base-skip-to-content: Accessibility skip link at the top of every page; jumps keyboard/screen-reader users past the header to the main content. Rendered before the message catalogue loads, so the server stamps it into the page rather than the app looking it up.
base-admin-badge: Small badge shown in the header on admin pages, indicating admin mode. Keep short.
base-log-out: Header button that signs the user out. Lowercase to match the compact header style.
base-admin-link: Header link to the admin dashboard, shown only to administrators. Lowercase to match the header style.
base-log-in: Header link to sign in (Wikimedia OAuth). Lowercase to match the header style.
base-dismiss: Accessible label (aria-label) for the × button that closes a toast/notification.
common-opens-in-new-tab: Visually-hidden suffix appended to links that open a new browser tab, for screen-reader users. Note the leading space.
home-timeline-aria: Accessible label for the small progress timeline on a consultation card showing which input phase it is in.
home-phase-explore:
Name of the first consultation phase (voting on statements). Also used in the phase legend and timeline.
{{Identical|Explore}}
home-phase-arguments:
Name of the arguments/argument-mapping phase. Used in the phase legend and timeline.
{{Identical|Arguments}}
home-phase-informed-vote:
Name of the informed-voting phase (a second voting round). Used in the phase legend and timeline.
{{Identical|Informed vote}}
home-phase-report:
Name of the final report/results phase. Used in the phase legend.
{{Identical|Report}}
home-phase-optin-id: Timeline step where participants may opt in to revealing their identity after a consultation closes.
home-outputs-aria: Accessible label for the grid of output symbols (report, data, etc.) on a consultation card.
home-chip-to-vote: Chip on a consultation card. $1 is the number of statements the user still has to vote on.
home-chip-next:
Chip on a consultation card announcing its next scheduled phase change, e.g. "Next: Informed vote 1 Oct 2026, 12:00". Parameters:
* $1 - the name of the next phase, e.g. {{msg-proto|phase-label-informed_voting}}
* $2 - the date and time, a <nowiki><time></nowiki> element formatted in the chosen language and the reader's timezone, with {{msg-proto|conv-scheduled-tz-title}} as its tooltip
The longer notice inside a consultation is {{msg-proto|conv-scheduled-transition}}.
home-chip-reveal-today: Chip warning that the identity-reveal window closes today.
home-chip-reveal-days: Chip warning how long the identity-reveal window stays open. $1 is a number of days; 'd' abbreviates 'days'.
home-chip-reveal-opens: Chip noting when the identity-reveal window will open. $1 is a number of days; 'd' abbreviates 'days'.
home-banner-prototype: Banner at the top of the landing page and the consultation list. $1 is a link labelled {{msg-proto|home-banner-open-issue}} that opens the issue tracker in a new tab.
home-banner-open-issue: Link text in the prototype banner to report a bug (opens the GitHub issue tracker).
home-hero-heading: Main heading on the signed-out landing page. The product's value proposition.
home-hero-body: Sub-heading paragraph on the signed-out landing page describing how the tool works.
home-login-wikimedia: Label on the button that starts Wikimedia OAuth login.
home-dev-badge: Label for the local-development-only login shortcuts. Only visible in dev mode.
home-dev-login-as: title attribute (tooltip) on a dev login shortcut. $1 is a username. Dev-only.
home-open-consultations: Section heading listing publicly-open consultations to signed-out visitors.
home-count-total: Count shown next to a section heading. $1 is the number of items.
home-card-join-aria: Accessible label for a consultation card link. $1 is the consultation title.
home-action-join: Call-to-action on a consultation card to join it. The arrow is decorative. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-action-continue: Call-to-action on a consultation card the user has already joined. The arrow is decorative. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-action-view: Call-to-action on a consultation card with nothing for the user to do: caught up, inactive or closed. Rendered in capitals by CSS; the arrow is decorative.
home-action-admin: Call-to-action to open the admin panel for a consultation the user moderates. The arrow is decorative. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-flow-alt: alt text for the diagram illustrating how a Proto consultation flows through its phases.
home-phase-legend-aria: Accessible label for the phase-journey legend diagram.
home-view-mode-aria: Accessible label for the toggle switching between the user's own consultations and browsing all.
home-mode-yours: Toggle button showing the consultations the signed-in user has joined.
home-mode-browse: Toggle button to browse all consultations open to the user.
home-heading: Visually hidden page heading of the consultation list, for screen readers.
home-section-closed:
Section heading for the user's closed consultations.
{{Identical|Closed}}
home-section-open-to-you: Section heading for consultations the user may join but has not yet.
home-section-moderate: Section heading listing consultations the user moderates/administers.
home-section-needs-attention: Section heading for the user's consultations where there is something for them to do, such as statements left to vote on. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-section-caught-up: Section heading for the user's consultations where they have voted on every statement for now. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-section-inactive: Section heading for the user's consultations that are paused, or in a phase with nothing for participants to do. Rendered in capitals by CSS; write it in sentence case.
home-card-aria-pseudonym: Fragment appended to a card's accessible label naming the user's pseudonym in that consultation. $1 is the pseudonym.
home-card-aria-remaining: Fragment appended to a card's accessible label with how many statements remain to vote. $1 is a number.
home-card-aria-continue: Fragment appended to an active card's accessible label indicating the action is to continue.
home-card-aria-closed: Fragment appended to a closed card's accessible label indicating it is closed.
home-card-aria-caught-up: Fragment appended to the accessible label of a consultation card in the {{msg-proto|home-section-caught-up}} section. Other fragments may precede it, such as {{msg-proto|home-card-aria-pseudonym}}; the dash separates it from them.
home-card-aria-inactive: Fragment appended to the accessible label of a consultation card in the {{msg-proto|home-section-inactive}} section. "Inactive" describes the consultation.
home-card-badge-closed:
Small badge marking a consultation as closed.
{{Identical|closed}}
home-card-badge-caught-up: Small badge on a consultation card: the user has voted on every statement available for now. Describes the user's state in that consultation.
home-card-badge-paused: Small badge on a consultation card: an organizer has paused the consultation. Describes the consultation.
home-card-badge-waiting: Small badge on a consultation card: the consultation is between phases, with nothing for participants to do until the next one opens. Describes the consultation.
home-card-view-aria: Accessible label for a moderated consultation's title link. $1 is the title.
home-card-admin-aria: Accessible label for the admin-panel link on a moderated consultation. $1 is the title.
home-empty-none-joined: Empty-state text when the user has joined no consultations.
home-empty-none-open: Empty-state text when no consultations are open to the user.
home-output-dialog-close: Accessible label for the button closing the output-details dialog.
home-output-dialog-title: Default title of the dialog explaining why a consultation output is not ready yet.
common-return-home: Generic link back to the home page. Arrow is decorative in the template.
common-checklist: Section heading for a checklist of guidance points.
forbidden-elig-doc-title: Browser tab title of the not-eligible page. $1 is the consultation title, which is organizer-authored content and stays untranslated.
forbidden-elig-heading: Main heading when a user cannot join a consultation because they fail its eligibility check.
forbidden-elig-requirement: The eligibility rule on the not-eligible page, when the organizer has not named the requirement. When they have, {{msg-proto|forbidden-elig-requirement-named}} is used instead.
forbidden-elig-unavailable: Shown when the external eligibility checker service is down.
forbidden-elig-criteria: Shown when the user's account does not satisfy the eligibility rules.
forbidden-invite-doc-title: Browser tab title of the invite-only refusal page, site name included.
forbidden-invite-heading: Main heading when a consultation is restricted to invited participants.
forbidden-invite-body: Whole sentence telling the visitor they are not on the invite list. $1 is the consultation title, shown in bold; it is organizer-authored content and stays untranslated. Keep the <nowiki><strong></nowiki> tags.
forbidden-invite-mod-lead: Bold lead-in shown to moderators on the invite-only page.
forbidden-invite-mod-body: Tells a moderator how to also join as a voter; a link follows.
forbidden-invite-mod-link: Link to the invite-management admin page. Arrow is decorative.
forbidden-invite-back-home: Low-emphasis link back to the home page. Arrow is decorative.
guidance-statement-doc-title:
Browser tab/title for the statement-writing guide. Followed by the site name.
{{Identical|Writing good statements}}
guidance-statement-crumb: Header breadcrumb label for the statement-writing guide.
guidance-statement-heading:
Main heading of the statement-writing guide.
{{Identical|Writing good statements}}
guidance-statement-intro: Intro paragraph of the statement-writing guide. 'Agree', 'Disagree', 'Pass' are the vote options.
guidance-statement-check-one-claim: Checklist item (contains bold lead). Advises one claim per statement. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-statement-check-neutral: Checklist item (contains bold lead). Advises neutral wording. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-statement-check-specific: Checklist item (contains bold lead). Advises specificity. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-statement-check-statement: Checklist item (contains bold lead). Advises writing a statement, not a question. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-statement-split-label: Bold label introducing an example of splitting compound claims.
guidance-statement-split-body: Example showing how to split a compound statement into two.
guidance-statement-questions-label: Bold label introducing an example of turning a question into a claim.
guidance-statement-questions-body: Example showing how to rewrite a rhetorical question as a claim.
guidance-statement-pass-heading: Heading for the section explaining when to use the Pass vote.
guidance-statement-pass-body: Paragraph explaining when passing on a statement is appropriate.
guidance-argument-doc-title:
Browser tab/title for the argument-writing guide. Followed by the site name.
{{Identical|Writing good arguments}}
guidance-argument-crumb: Header breadcrumb label for the argument-writing guide.
guidance-argument-heading:
Main heading of the argument-writing guide.
{{Identical|Writing good arguments}}
guidance-argument-intro: Intro paragraph of the argument-writing guide.
guidance-argument-check-direction: Checklist item (bold lead). Advises stating for/against. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-argument-check-reason: Checklist item (bold lead). Advises giving a reason. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-argument-check-one-point: Checklist item (bold lead). Advises one point per argument. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-argument-check-specific: Checklist item (bold lead). Advises specificity. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-argument-check-claim: Checklist item (bold lead). Advises against personal attacks. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
guidance-argument-weak-label: Bold label for a weak example argument.
guidance-argument-strong-label: Bold label for a stronger example argument.
guidance-argument-moderation-body: Paragraph on moderation expectations for arguments.
output-produced-suffix: Word after the phase name, forming e.g. 'Explore output'. The phase name is data.
output-howto-heading: Heading for the explanatory box on an output detail page.
output-produced-from: Definition-list term: which phase produced this output.
output-pending-suffix: Appended after the status when the output is not ready yet. Leading middle-dot separator.
output-method-label: Definition-list term: the method used to produce the output.
output-initial-clustering-heading: Section heading for the initial-clustering output.
output-initial-clustering-body: Placeholder description of the initial-clustering output.
output-initial-clustering-note: Italic note that the clustering visuals are not built yet.
output-argument-map-heading: Section heading for the argument-map output.
output-argument-map-body: Placeholder description of the argument-map output.
output-argument-map-link: Link to the Arguments tab of the live consultation. Arrow follows in the template.
output-preliminary-heading: Section heading for the preliminary-results output.
output-preliminary-body: Placeholder description of the preliminary-results output.
output-preliminary-link: Link to the preliminary-results tab of the live consultation. Arrow follows in the template.
output-dataset-heading: Section heading for the dataset output.
output-dataset-body: Placeholder description of the dataset output. 'xid' is an internal pseudonymous id; keep as-is.
output-dataset-note: Italic note that the dataset export is not built yet.
output-tbd-heading: Fallback section heading for an output type with no bespoke description yet.
common-days: Pluralized unit 'day(s)'. $1 is the number; used after a number rendered separately.
reveal-crumb: Header breadcrumb label for the identity-reveal page.
reveal-banner-identity: Small banner label above the identity-reveal page headings.
reveal-banner-window: Banner label (lowercase) on the active reveal-window form.
reveal-linked-heading: Heading shown after the user has linked their identity.
reveal-label-pseudonym: Field label for the participant's pseudonym in the identity card.
reveal-label-username: Field label for the participant's Wikimedia username in the identity card.
reveal-permanent-note: Note under the identity card explaining the link is permanent.
reveal-closed-heading: Heading when the reveal window has already closed.
reveal-closed-body: Body when the reveal window has closed.
reveal-notyet-heading: Heading when the reveal window has not opened yet.
reveal-notyet-body: Body when the window is not open; an exact date and a period follow in the template.
reveal-notyet-after: Explanatory note (contains bold 'permanently'); no parameters. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
reveal-open-heading-a: First half of the reveal heading; the participant's pseudonym follows.
reveal-open-heading-b: Second half of the reveal heading, after the pseudonym.
reveal-open-body-a: Start of the reveal explanation; the Wikimedia username follows.
reveal-open-body-b: Connective between the username and the pseudonym in the reveal explanation.
reveal-open-body-c: End of the reveal explanation, after the pseudonym.
reveal-irreversible-label: Bold warning label above the irreversible-consequences list.
reveal-irrev-li1-a: Start of the first irreversible-consequences bullet; the username (in parentheses) follows.
reveal-irrev-li1-b: Middle of the first bullet, between the username and the pseudonym.
reveal-irrev-li1-c: End of the first bullet, after the pseudonym.
reveal-consent-a: Start of the consent checkbox label; the username (in parentheses) follows.
reveal-consent-b: Middle of the consent label, between the username and the pseudonym (in parentheses).
reveal-submit: Submit button confirming the irreversible identity link.
reveal-tl-aria: Accessible label for the three-step reveal timeline.
reveal-tl-closed-what: Timeline node: consultation closed; $1 is the cooldown length in days.
reveal-tl-step-inprogress: Screen-reader-only status for the cooldown step when it is current.
reveal-tl-step-completed:
Screen-reader-only status for a timeline step that is done.
{{Identical|(completed)}}
reveal-tl-opens-what: Timeline node: reveal window opens; $1 is the window length in days.
reveal-tl-step-current: Screen-reader-only status for the current timeline step.
reveal-tl-step-upcoming:
Screen-reader-only status for an upcoming timeline step.
{{Identical|(upcoming)}}
reveal-tl-deadline-opens: Countdown line on the identity-reveal timeline while the window is still pending. $1 is the remaining time, supplied already styled.
reveal-tl-deadline-closes: Countdown line on the identity-reveal timeline once the window has opened or been used. $1 is the remaining time, supplied already styled. Use reveal-tl-deadline-closes-permanent for the state where linking is still possible. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
reveal-tl-deadline-closes-permanent: Countdown line on the identity-reveal timeline while the window is open, so the warning that linking cannot be undone sits in the same sentence as the deadline. $1 is the remaining time. Used instead of reveal-tl-deadline-closes in that one state. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
reveal-tl-days: Server-rendered countdown fallback; $1 is a number of days. Replaced live by a ticking clock in JS.
reveal-tl-now: JS countdown text once the deadline is reached.
accept-crumb: Header breadcrumb label for the join/accept page.
accept-joining: Small label above the consultation title on the join page.
accept-reroll-aria: Accessible label for the reroll button.
accept-reroll: Reroll button text; the ↻ glyph regenerates pseudonym options.
accept-reroll-loading: Reroll button text while new options are loading.
accept-pseudonym-help: Helper text under the pseudonym-picker title.
accept-notify-email: Checkbox label opting into email notifications.
accept-notify-email-unavailable: Shown instead of the email-notification checkbox when the account has no confirmed email address. $1 is a link to Wikimedia account preferences, labelled {{msg-proto|accept-notify-add-email}}, which opens in a new tab.
accept-notify-add-email: Link text inside {{msg-proto|accept-notify-email-unavailable}}, leading to Wikimedia account preferences. "One" is a confirmed email address.
accept-notify-talk: Checkbox label opting into talk-page notifications.
accept-privacy-details-summary: Summary/label of the expandable privacy details.
accept-privacy-body1: First paragraph of the expanded privacy details.
accept-privacy-body2: Second paragraph of the expanded privacy details.
accept-privacy-reveal-window:
The identity-reveal window, in the privacy details on the join screen. Parameters:
* $1 - the number of days after close when the window opens, e.g. 30
* $2 - the number of days after close when it shuts, e.g. 60
Keep the <nowiki><strong></nowiki> tags.
accept-licence-heading: Heading of the content-licence section on the join screen. Sits between the privacy summary and the consent checkbox.
accept-licence-intro: Licence disclosure on the join screen. $1 is a link to the CC0 deed, labelled with {{msg-proto|accept-licence-link}}. Do not translate the licence name itself.
accept-licence-link: Link label for the CC0 1.0 deed, used as $1 in {{msg-proto|accept-licence-intro}}. This is a licence name; keep it as-is.
accept-licence-scope: Second paragraph of the licence disclosure, shown muted. Explains that the licence covers the text and not attribution, that votes are excluded, and that the grant is irrevocable. This is an enforceable legal statement -- translate precisely and do not soften or omit any clause.
accept-consent: Label of the required consent checkbox on the join screen. This is the enforceable consent statement -- it must state all three clauses (pseudonymous record, internal username link, CC0 release). Do not shorten.
accept-submit: Submit button on the join screen. $1 is the pseudonym the participant has selected, e.g. "quiet-otter"; it is participant data and stays untranslated, and updates as they pick another. The arrow is decorative.
accept-not-now: Low-emphasis link to leave without joining.
accept-js-selected: Screen-reader announcement after choosing a pseudonym; $1 is the name.
accept-js-regenerated: Screen-reader announcement after rerolling; $1 is the newly selected name.
reveal-callout-open-text: Callout shown while the identity-reveal window is open. $1 is the participant’s pseudonym, shown in bold, and is not translated. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
reveal-callout-link: Link in the reveal callout to the identity-linking page. Arrow follows in the template.
report-crumb: Header breadcrumb label for the final report page.
report-subtitle: Subtitle under the report title; a closed-date suffix may follow.
report-closed-suffix: Suffix before the consultation's close date in the report subtitle. Leading middle-dot.
report-badge-final: Badge marking the report as the final, frozen version.
report-status-final: Status value in the report's how-to-read box.
report-intro-heading: Section heading for the report introduction.
report-intro-placeholder: Italic placeholder where the organizer introduction will go.
report-process-heading: Section heading for the consultation process timeline.
report-process-opened: Timeline label: when the consultation opened.
report-process-submission: Timeline label for the submission phase.
report-process-dates-tbd: Placeholder where a phase's dates are not recorded yet.
report-process-argmap:
Timeline label for the argument-mapping phase.
{{Identical|Argument mapping}}
report-process-informed:
Timeline label for the informed-voting phase.
{{Identical|Informed voting}}
report-process-closed: Timeline label: when the consultation closed.
report-participation-p2: Stat label: participant count in the initial voting round.
report-participation-p6: Stat label: participant count in the informed voting round.
report-participation-both: Stat label: participants who voted in both rounds (placeholder).
report-moderation-applied: Lead-in before counts of moderation exclusions.
report-moderation-stmts: Count of statements excluded by moderation. $1 is the number.
report-moderation-parts: Count of participants excluded by moderation. Leading middle-dot separator; $1 is the number.
report-participation-unavailable: Shown when the results database cannot be reached.
report-statements-heading:
Section heading for the statement inventory.
{{Identical|Statements}}
report-statements-placeholder: Italic placeholder for the statement inventory.
report-featured-count: Count of featured statements. $1 is the number.
report-initial-heading: Section heading for the initial (Phase 2) opinions.
report-bar-title: Tooltip on a vote bar. $1, $2 and $3 are the agree, disagree and pass percentages.
report-bar-label: Label under a vote bar. $1 is the agree percentage, $2 the pass percentage, $3 the number of votes.
report-most-divisive: Sub-heading listing the most divisive statements.
report-argmap-heading:
Section heading for the argument-mapping summary.
{{Identical|Argument mapping}}
report-argmap-placeholder: Italic placeholder for the argument-mapping summary.
report-shift-heading: Section heading for the aggregate opinion-shift analysis.
report-shift-intro: Intro paragraph above the opinion-shift table. $1 is a link to the Methodology section of the same report, labelled with {{msg-proto|report-methodology-link}} — e.g. Methodology. The parenthetical used to be three separate messages, which fixed the English word order; it is one sentence now, so move "$1" and "below" wherever your language needs them. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
report-methodology-link:
Link text pointing to the Methodology section.
{{Identical|Methodology}}
report-shift-sorted: Note that the opinion-shift table is sorted by shift magnitude.
report-col-statement:
Table column header: the statement text.
{{Identical|Statement}}
report-col-shift:
Table column header: the opinion shift.
{{Identical|Shift}}
report-col-shift-note: Small note under the Shift column header clarifying it is an aggregate.
report-table-aria: Accessible label for the opinion-shift table.
report-matched-heading: Section heading for the matched-participant delta analysis.
report-matched-placeholder: Italic placeholder for the matched-participant analysis.
report-matched-note: Caveat about the matched-participant delta and extrapolation.
report-groups-heading: Section heading for the opinion-group clusters.
report-groups-sub: Sub-label with the number of opinion groups. $1 is the count.
report-group-label: Heading for a single opinion group. $1 is the group number.
report-group-members: Member count for an opinion group. Leading middle-dot; $1 is the number.
report-badge-agree:
Badge marking a statement the group agreed with.
{{Identical|agree}}
report-badge-disagree:
Badge marking a statement the group disagreed with.
{{Identical|disagree}}
report-landed-heading: Heading of the personalised self-comparison section.
report-landed-body: Placeholder body for the personalised self-comparison.
report-methodology-heading:
Section heading for the methodology explanation.
{{Identical|Methodology}}
report-methodology-sources-body: Data-sources methodology paragraph (contains an inline code span for a DB view name). Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
report-methodology-shift-body: Methodology paragraph for the aggregate shift (contains inline em and bold). Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
report-methodology-delta-body: Methodology paragraph for individual delta and extrapolation.
report-methodology-delta-placeholder: Italic placeholder for the CI methodology.
report-methodology-clustering-body: Methodology paragraph for the clustering algorithm.
report-no-results: Shown when there are no informed-voting results to report.
conv-crumb-aria: Accessible label for the header breadcrumb on a consultation page.
conv-crumb-about: Header breadcrumb link from the conversation workspace to the consultation’s about page.
conv-crumb-manage: Header link for moderators to open the admin view of this consultation.
conv-noun-statement: The word 'statement' used as a noun inside the flag control (e.g. 'flag concerns about this statement').
conv-noun-argument: The word 'argument' used as a noun inside the flag control.
conv-flag-aria: Accessible label for the flag control. $1 is the thing being flagged (statement/argument).
conv-flag-summary: Toggle text opening the flag form. $1 is the thing being flagged.
conv-flag-reason-label:
Hidden label for the flag-category dropdown.
{{Identical|Reason}}
conv-flag-details-label: Hidden label for the optional flag-details textarea.
conv-flag-details-placeholder: Placeholder for the optional flag-details textarea.
conv-demo-label:
Bold label marking a demo consultation.
{{Identical|Demo}}
conv-demo-text: Explanation of demo mode, after the bold 'Demo' label.
conv-space-warn-live-label: Bold lead-in of the banner shown when a participant lands on a REAL consultation they did not explicitly choose. Must read as a warning that this is the genuine thing, never as a demo. Pairs with conv-space-warn-live-body.
conv-space-warn-live-body: Body of the same real-consultation banner: tells the participant their votes are counted, then invites anyone only exploring to leave for the demo. Keep as one sentence pair; a translation must not suggest the votes are practice ones. Followed by conv-space-warn-live-link.
conv-space-warn-live-link: Link at the end of the real-consultation banner, offering the demo space to someone who only wanted to look around.
conv-space-warn-demo-label: Bold lead-in of the banner shown when a participant lands on a DEMONSTRATION consultation. Must read as "not real", never as a live consultation. Pairs with conv-space-warn-demo-body.
conv-space-warn-demo-body: Body of the same demo banner: tells the participant nothing cast here counts. Keep as one sentence; a translation must not let it be read as a live consultation. Followed by conv-space-warn-demo-link.
conv-space-warn-demo-link: Link at the end of the demo banner, leading to the index of demonstration consultations.
conv-space-warn-ok: Button that dismisses the real/demo banner for this visit. Acknowledgement, not consent.
conv-demo-mode-lock: Persistent notice at the top of every demonstration consultation, unlike the dismissible banner. Says the mechanics behave normally while the consultation itself is not real; a translation must keep both halves.
conv-scheduled-transition: Notice above a consultation whose next phase change is already scheduled. $1 is the name of the phase it moves to, shown in bold; $2 is the date and time, already formatted in the reader’s own timezone. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
conv-scheduled-tz-title: Tooltip on the date of the next scheduled phase change, telling the reader the time is converted to their own timezone.
conv-closed-on: Opening paragraph on a closed consultation: says when it closed and that votes were recorded pseudonymously, with a window to link a username later. $1 is the close date, shown in bold. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
conv-revealed-text: Shown to a participant who has already linked their identity. $1 is their pseudonym, shown in bold, and is not translated. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
conv-reveal-pending-opens: Shown while the identity-reveal window is still sealed. $1 is the date it opens.
conv-reveal-expired: Shown when the identity-reveal window has expired.
conv-closed-simple: Simple closed-state message when no reveal context applies.
conv-read-report: Link to the final report: on the informed-voting done screen after {{msg-proto|conv-p6-done-closed}}, and on its own in a closed consultation. A decorative arrow follows.
conv-paused: Shown when a consultation is paused.
conv-nothing-available: Shown when no participation tab is available yet.
conv-tab-vote: Tab label for the voting phase.
conv-tab-results: Tab label for the intermediate results.
conv-tab-arguments:
Tab label for the argument-mapping phase.
{{Identical|Arguments}}
conv-tab-informed:
Tab label for the informed-voting phase.
{{Identical|Informed vote}}
conv-tab-preliminary:
Tab label (and section label) for preliminary informed-voting results.
{{Identical|Preliminary results}}
conv-vote-voted-label: Label after the 'done / total' count in the vote progress row.
conv-vote-progress-aria:

adminconv-countdown-days: Compact day unit in the countdown to a scheduled phase transition, e.g. "2d 4h 30m". $1 is the number of days. Keep it to a letter or two.
adminconv-countdown-hours: Compact hour unit in the countdown to a scheduled phase transition. $1 is the number of hours. Keep it to a letter or two.
adminconv-countdown-minutes: Compact minute unit in the countdown to a scheduled phase transition. $1 is the number of minutes. Keep it to a letter or two.
adminconv-countdown-lt1m: Countdown shown when a scheduled transition is under a minute away but not yet due; the other units are {{msg-proto|adminconv-countdown-minutes}} and its siblings. Keep it very short, in words, e.g. "under 1 min". Do not use <nowiki><</nowiki>: the message cannot be parsed with it. Do not use an HTML entity either: the countdown is plain text, so it would show literally.
adminconv-status-published: Pill beside the report phase name: the final report has been published.
adminconv-status-unpublished: Pill beside the report phase name: the report phase is reached but the report has not been published.
adminconv-phase-desc-published: Description under the current-phase name once the report is published, replacing the phase effect text.
adminconv-report-published-note: Note in place of the move-on box when there is nothing left to advance to and the report is published. The <nowiki><strong></nowiki> emphasis is part of the sentence.
adminconv-report-unpublished-note: Note in place of the move-on box when the report phase is reached but not published; points the organizer at the publish control lower down. The <nowiki><strong></nowiki> emphasis is part of the sentence.
adminconv-roles-summary-count: Disclosure summary for the roles list when roles are assigned. $1 is how many.
adminconv-assigned-count: Count badge on the "Roles" card of the admin console. $1 is the number of role assignments in this consultation, e.g. 4.
adminconv-publish-irrev: Warning under the publish-report control once the cleanup window is open. $1 is the report URL path; the <nowiki><code></nowiki> markup around it is part of the message.
adminconv-closed-on: Opens the danger-zone description of a closed consultation. $1 is the close date. A sentence about the identity-reveal window follows.
adminconv-closed-undated: Used instead of adminconv-closed-on when no close date was recorded.
adminconv-reveal-pending: Danger-zone description when the identity-reveal window has not opened yet. $1 is the opening date, $2 the number of days until then.
adminconv-reveal-open-date: Danger-zone description while the identity-reveal window is open. $1 is the closing date.
base-mode-switch-aria: Accessible name for the demo/real toggle in the site header. Names the choice, since the two options alone do not say what is being switched.
base-mode-demo: The demo option in the header's demo/real toggle. A call to action, not a noun — it invites the visitor into a practice consultation. Sits beside {{msg-proto|base-mode-real}}.
base-mode-real: The real-consultation option in the header's demo/real toggle, beside {{msg-proto|base-mode-demo}}. Short because it is one half of a two-option switch.
base-lock-real: Badge in the header of a real consultation, marking that what the participant does here counts. The demo counterpart is {{msg-proto|conv-demo-label}}.
base-footer-licence: Licence line in the site footer. $1 is a link to the CC0 deed labelled with {{msg-proto|accept-licence-link}} — e.g. CC0. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
fork-demo-title: Heading of the card leading to a demonstration consultation.
fork-demo-sub: Subtitle under {{msg-proto|fork-demo-title}}: what the demo card offers.
fork-demo-cta: Call to action on the demo card. The arrow is decorative.
fork-demo-aria: Accessible name for the whole demo card, which is one link. Says both the heading and the subtitle, since a screen-reader user hears the link name in place of the card.
fork-real-title: Heading of the card leading to live consultations.
fork-real-sub: Subtitle under {{msg-proto|fork-real-title}}: the point of difference from the demo card.
fork-real-cta: Call to action on the real-consultations card. The arrow is decorative.
fork-real-aria: Accessible name for the whole real-consultations card, which is one link.
base-language-label: Accessible name for the language switcher in the site header. The options are language autonyms and are never translated — a reader looking for Dutch scans for "Nederlands".
base-loading-conversations: Shown while the app is still fetching. It renders before the message catalogue has loaded, so the server stamps it into the page; see {{msg-proto|base-skip-to-content}}, which is delivered the same way.
errorpage-code: Small label above the heading on a server error page. $1 is the HTTP status code, e.g. 404.
errorpage-404-hint: What to do next, on the 404 page. Keep the HTML and the text inside it — it links to the front page.
errorpage-403-title: Heading of the 403 page. An adjective describing the request, not the person.
errorpage-403-hint: What to do next, on the 403 page.
errorpage-500-hint: What to do next, on the 500 page.
accept-js-taken: Live-region announcement when the chosen pseudonym was claimed by someone else between the page loading and the form being submitted. Fresh options are offered.
forbidden-elig-requirement-named: The eligibility rule on the not-eligible page, when the organizer named one. $1 is that name, shown in bold — organizer-authored content, so it stays untranslated. When no name is configured, {{msg-proto|forbidden-elig-requirement}} is used instead. Keep the HTML and the text inside it.
